ExecutionBlockNumberOrTag.title: executionBlockNumberOrTag
ExecutionBlockNumberOrTag.description:
A block to execute against, given as its height in hex or in decimal, or as a tag. The decimal form is accepted because the block is resolved by `ExecutionBlockRetriever`, which parses both bases; the block-reading methods resolve through `Web3InformationRetriever`, which parses hex only and answers `invalid blocknumber` for a decimal height. It is not the only place decimal is taken -- `eth_getBlocksByNumber` parses its own height and accepts both bases too -- but among the methods that take a block parameter it is what separates executing from reading.

As for the reading methods, a string of `0x` and exactly 64 hex digits is always read as a 32-byte block hash, never as a height, so a height zero-padded to that length is not accepted. The hash is left out of the union above for the same reason it is left out of `blockNumberOrTag`.
